name: Aluminium Fluoride (AlF3): Smelter Flux Import Substitution from Fertiliser Fluorine By-Product
scope: India's primary aluminium smelting capacity is being expanded sharply (Hindalco ~Rs 21,000 cr / 3.6 lakh tpa Aditya expansion announced Jan 2026; Vedanta/BALCO growth; NALCO smelter 460k to ~960k tpa), and AlF3, the essential smelter bath flux, is made domestically by fewer than five firms and supplemented by imports; Alufluoride completed a 24,000 tpa expansion (Jun 2026), Paradeep Phosphates' board approved a Rs 250 cr / 15,000 tpa AlF3 plant (28 Jul 2026) and NALCO invited JV/partner EoIs for AlF3 (issued 21 Sep, closed 12 Oct 2026); it is a niche chemical with thin theme-level coverage, though Paradeep already jumped ~15% on the plant news and Alufluoride is volatile and supply-constrained, so it is early rather than fully undiscovered.
questions: What is aluminium fluoride (AlF3), how much is consumed per tonne of primary aluminium, and what is the current global and Indian demand, price and import-dependence picture (including any China pricing or export influence)?

How does the fertiliser by-product route work (hydrofluosilicic acid/FSA from phosphoric acid plants reacted with alumina hydrate), and what limits supply of FSA and other inputs (e.g. West Asia/Hormuz disruption to sulphur and ammonia in 2026)?

How large is the coming Indian smelter capacity build-out (Hindalco Aditya expansion, Vedanta/BALCO, NALCO 460k to ~960k tpa), by when, and what incremental AlF3 demand does it imply versus current domestic capacity?

What exactly has Alufluoride done (24,000 tpa expansion completed Jun 2026, FSA supply contracts with IFFCO Paradeep and others, Q1 FY27 revenue fall from supply disruption, NSE listing Aug 2026) and how reliable are its volumes, customers and margins?

What are Paradeep Phosphates' AlF3 plans (Rs 250 cr, 15,000 tpa, ~22-24 months to commission, targeted Rs 180-200 cr revenue and ~Rs 50 cr EBITDA), and how material is this to a company with ~Rs 6,000 cr quarterly revenue and fertiliser-subsidy exposure?

What is the AlF3 position of SPIC (Greenstar, supplies Hindalco/Dubal) and Tanfac (AlF3 listed among its products; separate Rs 495 cr fluorinated chemicals expansion) - capacity, share of revenue and any announced AlF3 expansion - and is AlF3 a meaningful earnings driver for either?
What is NALCO's AlF3/CPC/coal-tar-pitch backward-integration plan (EoI closed 12 Oct 2026), who responded, and could fertiliser or fluorine-chemical listed firms become JV partners or suppliers?

Have the stocks already re-rated and has mainstream media or broker research grouped these names as an AlF3 theme (Paradeep ~+15% on 29 Jul 2026 and ~+38-42% in six months but down over one year; Alufluoride ~+40% to Apr 2026 peak then retraced)?

What are the risks: input (FSA) shortages, volatile AlF3 pricing and Chinese competition, customer concentration in Hindalco/Vedanta/NALCO, smelter project delays, execution and commissioning slippage, and small-cap liquidity?

What are the catalysts over the next 6-12 months: NALCO EoI outcome, Paradeep and other fertiliser makers' plant progress, smelter commissioning dates, any anti-dumping or import-duty action on AlF3, and quarterly volume recovery at Alufluoride?
